sentences.text: It possesses a proportionally smaller humerus with a wider upper end than any living owl, a feature also observed in Ypresiglaux.
The tarsometatarsus – the fused foot bones – is short and robust, resembling that of the genus Minerva.
The first and second toe claws are markedly larger than the third and fourth, a trait characteristic of the family Protostrigidae.
All tail feathers are of similar length, lacking the rounded tail and barred pattern typical of modern owls.
The specimen preserves the first owl fossil with well-preserved feathers on both tail and wings.
Gerald Mayr and colleagues formally described Masillastrix blattophaga as a new genus and species in 2026.
Phylogenetic analysis places Masillastrix within the owl stem group, outside the crown group of modern owls, in an unresolved clade with Minerva and Oligostrix.
It is assigned to the family Protostrigidae within the class Aves.
Masillastrix lived during the Middle Eocene.
The known fossil occurrence dates to the Lutetian stage, about 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
